objective: Grow the records registry into a searchable library of at least 100 relevant records, with sixteen featured, without making any public read slower than today's.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: EVENTS-011 has merged to main. Test-first: commit the failing tests alone before the implementation; the implementation commit edits no test.

RECORDS holds at least 100 definitions, including every id in the brief's library table, each with a value_kind and a rule stating its counting window and any minimum. All twelve existing ids still resolve and mean the same thing, apart from their value_kind.

Every record has a category, one of team-franchise, team-season, team-game, player-game, player-season, player-career or player-playoffs, and a non-empty keywords list. A shooting record's keywords include the spellings fans use, so 3pt, three, threes and 3-pointer all match the threes records.
Exactly sixteen records have a featured_rank, 1 to 16, unique, in the order the brief lists them.

For each of field goals, threes and free throws, and at each of game, season and career scope, two records exist: the highest total (made_total: value is made, with attempted and pct) and the best percentage above a stated minimum of attempts (shot_pct: value is pct, with made and attempted). Minimums are the brief's, stated in the rule text, and a line or player under the minimum is never listed.

GET /events/records returns the whole catalog, {since_season, through_season, records: [{id, group, category, title, unit, rule, value_kind, keywords, featured_rank}]}, with no holder and exactly one database statement.

GET /events/records/holders?ids=a,b,c returns {holders: {id: holder or null}} for 1 to 24 distinct known ids. More than 24 ids, none, a duplicate or an unknown id is a 422. It runs at most 1 + the number of ids statements, each fetching at most one row.

GET /events/records/holders is declared before /events/records/{record_id}, answers Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, reads no user dependency, and test_records_contract.py pins all three. An unknown id on /events/records/{record_id} is still a 404.

infra/lib/cdn-stack.ts adds ids to both the records cache policy and the origin request policy allow lists. infra/test/cdn-stack.test.ts proves that two different ids values are separate cache entries and that no header or cookie joins the key. A 200 for ids=a must never answer ids=b.

Two tables, player_season_totals and team_game_totals, each with a bigint identity primary key, hold the aggregates the new records read. Written by one function, rebuild_record_totals(session), which replaces their contents in the caller's transaction. The Alembic migration creates and populates them and downgrades cleanly.

Every path that writes games or box scores calls rebuild_record_totals in the same transaction: load_nba_history, load_handler, seed_dev and the scale fixture. A test proves that a load which adds a game changes a season total, and that a failed load leaves the old totals.

Measured on the full dataset or the scale fixture on the db.t4g.micro proxy (--cpus=1 --memory=1g), and reported per route in the PR: the catalog at most 20 ms median; 24 holders at most 400 ms median, the featured 16 included; every list at most 300 ms median. Upgrade time and table sizes are reported too. Any new index names the statement it serves, in test_records_indexes.py.

The Records screen keeps working at this commit: until FRONTEND-030 merges the frontend reads holders through the new route with no visual change. Its tests pass after only their request mocks change.
backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts are regenerated. No new dependency.
frontend/src/test/bundle-budgets/EVENTS-012.ts declares every output the unit changes. Entry growth is at most 2 KiB raw and 1 KiB gzip, and no output reaches 500,000 raw bytes.
wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x02-events.md replaces 'Computed live: no aggregate table' with the new rule and these measurements, and lists the routes as built.
